title: Latency-aware fair queue and adaptive rate allocator for dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets currently use static rate caps and coarse queue depth controls that protect latency SLOs under common traffic patterns but struggle with mixed-criticality workloads and sudden cross-customer bursts. This ticket proposes a latency-aware fair queue combined with an adaptive rate allocator that dynamically reassigns throughput headroom across customers and routes while integrating with autoscaling signals.

Goals: 1) Maintain p95 latency SLOs for latency-sensitive routes while preserving throughput for best-effort workloads. 2) Improve utilization by allowing transient headroom sharing and reclaiming it predictably. 3) Provide operator-friendly knobs and observability for rollout and debugging.

High-level design: - Per-fleet admission controller composed of two cooperating components: (A) Latency-Aware Priority Queue (LAPQ) that enqueues requests into priority lanes (high/normal/low) with dynamic dequeue thresholds tuned to maintain measured percentiles; (B) Adaptive Rate Allocator (ARA) that periodically computes per-customer rate allocations based on configured guarantees, recent consumption, latency pressure signals, and autoscaler capacity forecasts. - LAPQ uses tokenized dequeue credits per lane. Credits regenerate at lane allocation rate from ARA and are consumed at request dispatch. When high-lane latency approaches threshold, LAPQ reduces normal/low dequeue share and issues preemptive backpressure (HTTP 429 with Retry-After when possible). - ARA inputs: configured guarantees (min throughput), burst allowances, recent usage windows (1s, 10s, 1m), measured latency percentiles per route, current executor headroom, and autoscaler predicted capacity delta. It outputs short-term allocations (1s-10s) and medium-term targets (30s-2m). - Admission policy DSL: extend existing fleet config with fields: guarantees:{min_rps}, burst:{burst_tokens,window_s}, priorities:{route->lane}, allocation_strategy:{mode:proportional|latency_first|strict_guarantee}, preemption_policy:{allow_reclaim:true|false, grace_ms}. - Autoscaler integration: ARA exposes unmet_demand and reclaimable_headroom metrics consumed by autoscaler. Autoscaler can proactively scale when unmet_demand > threshold for X seconds; conversely, ARA can probe reclaimable headroom before shrinking capacity.

Operator UX: - Configurable SLO mapping per route (latency percentile and target). - Console dashboard with per-fleet allocations, lane utilization, p50/p95/p99 latency per lane, token refill rates, and recent preemptions. - Escalation/diagnostic view that shows which customers consumed reclaimed headroom and why.

Acceptance criteria: - Under mixed workloads (latency-sensitive small inference + background long-batch embeds), p95 of high lane remains <= target 120ms in 95% of 10-minute windows for target fleet sizes. - Utilization increases by >=6% on synthetic burst tests versus baseline static caps without P95 regressions for high lane. - No customer experiences sustained starvation for more than grace window unless explicitly misconfigured. - Clear telemetry: new metrics emitted (list below) and dashboards created.

Implementation plan (phases): 1) Simulation & offline model (2w): build a traffic simulator and validate heuristics for ARA allocation strategies. 2) In-process LAPQ prototype (2w): implement queue + crediting in serving runtime behind a feature flag. 3) ARA service + autoscaler hooks (3w): standalone allocator that publishes allocations via control plane; autoscaler integration tests. 4) Canary rollout to a small dedicated fleet and real traffic test (2w): observe metrics and refine. 5) Gradual ramp to remaining fleets with operator controls.

Key metrics (new telemetry keys): - admission.lapq.lane.p95_latency_ms - admission.lapq.lane.dequeue_rate - admission.ara.reclaimable_headroom_rps - admission.ara.unmet_demand_rps - admission.preemptions.count - admission.backpressure.responses.429 - admission.queue.depth.by_lane

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: - We prefer soft preemption (429 + Retry-After) to aggressive request killing to preserve client retries and observability. - ARA uses multiple time windows to balance reactive short-term fairness with medium-term guarantees; tuning will likely need production traces. - Complexity tradeoff: central ARA simplifies global fairness but adds a control-plane dependency; design includes local fallback allocator when ARA control plane is unreachable (local proportional allocation based on static guarantees). - Security/tenant isolation: Reclaimed headroom must not leak customer-specific state; allocations are aggregated and applied as numeric tokens.

Rollout & safety: - Start with conservative allocation_strategy: latency_first and small burst allowances. - Add kill-switch feature flag per-fleet to revert to current static caps. - Add alerting on preemption spikes and unexpected unmet_demand growth.

Docs & artifacts: - PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Latency-aware+Fair+Queue+and+Adaptive+Rate+Allocator - Design notes & simulator: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ra-admission-sim - Initial implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7421 - Dashboard mockup: https://figma.com/file/Redwood/admission-control-dashboard Mockups and config schema included in PR.

Risk & mitigation: - Risk: mis-tuning ARA causes oscillation with autoscaler -> mitigation: smoothing, holdout timers, canarying, and conservative thresholds. - Risk: increased tail due to queueing delays -> mitigation: lane-level timers and max-queue-time eviction. - Risk: operator confusion -> mitigation: clear defaults, visualizations, and an "explain allocation" API returning rationale for recent decisions.
comments: 2026-02-25 Ava Chen: Triage note - picked up from backlog; initial spike to validate simulation approach. Assigned to Diego for prototyping.

2026-03-01 Diego Martínez: Completed simulator and ran baseline comparisons for proportional vs latency_first strategies. Results: latency_first kept p95 stable but underutilized headroom during very bursty background job. Noted need for hybrid heuristics.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed tradeoffs. Suggested adding a DBA-style grace window to avoid immediate preemption for customers with short sustained bursts (10s). Also requested dashboard mockups for product review.
2026-03-06 Elena Rossi (Design): Uploaded dashboard mockups and suggested telemetry grouping by tenant and route in the Console. Added notes about wording for preemption alerts.

2026-03-09 Diego Martínez: LAPQ prototype merged behind feature flag in serving runtime. Basic metrics emitted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7421. Integration tests added for token accounting.

2026-03-11 QA: Ran canary synthetic traffic for 12h. High-priority route p95 remained under SLO in 98% windows. Observed one oscillation event coinciding with autoscaler latency; added smoothing to ARA outputs.
2026-03-13 Security review kickoff: security flagged the need to document allocation ACLs and ensure control plane RPCs authenticate via mTLS. Diego to add ACL doc and audit logs.
2026-03-13 PM note: Plan to schedule a 1-week canary on fleet-qa with ops-runbook and alerting before broader rollout.
